title: Taiwan’s two-speed AI economy
gist: Taiwan's AI boom produced 15% annualised Q1 2026 growth with full-year GDP projected up to 10% and a stock market now larger than India's or the UK's, driven by TSMC and a supplier base that builds around 90% of the world's AI servers. But excluding semiconductors and AI servers, Taiwanese exports have fallen 40% since 2022, and roughly 80% of exports now sit in the AI hardware category versus half pre-pandemic — a concentration that makes Taiwan a linchpin of US economic growth and simultaneously hostage to any drawdown in US AI capex.

insights.claim: Taiwan's economy grew at a 15% annualised clip in Q1 2026, with full-year 2026 GDP growth projected to reach up to 10% — rates not seen since Taiwan's economic miracle era.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: A developed economy printing double-digit growth off one sector is the clearest macro read-through of the AI capex cycle available anywhere.
insights.quote: Taiwan’s economy grew at a stupendous 15% (Opens in new window) clip in the first quarter of this year on an annualised basis.
insights.locator: In this regard, Taiwan has thrown up a doozy

insights.claim: Taiwan's stock market has now surpassed both the Indian and UK bourses in value.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: A concrete index-weight milestone: Taiwan's rising share of global and EM benchmarks raises passive investors' unhedged exposure to a single geopolitical flashpoint.
insights.quote: Taiwan’s stock market has now surpassed both (Opens in new window) the Indian and UK bourses in value
insights.locator: Adding to the surreality is the fact

insights.claim: Nvidia has taken the baton from Apple as TSMC's largest customer, and TSMC is also a crucial supplier for companies seeking to challenge or reduce their dependence on Nvidia.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: TSMC captures value on both sides of the accelerator war — a structurally hedged position regardless of which chip designer wins share.
insights.quote: Nvidia has now taken the baton from Apple as TSMC’s (Opens in new window) largest customer.
insights.locator: TSMC makes most (Opens in new window) of Nvidia’s silicon

insights.claim: Taiwan's AI supply chain role extends well beyond TSMC to firms including Foxconn, Wistron, Quanta Computer and Delta Electronics, which build AI servers, GPU modules and cooling solutions — with Taiwan making around 90% of the world's AI servers.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: Names the second-tier Taiwanese beneficiaries of AI capex — server, GPU module and cooling suppliers with a near-monopoly share often missed in TSMC-focused analysis.
insights.quote: Taiwan also makes around (Opens in new window) 90% of the world’s AI servers
insights.locator: When Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang visited Taiwan

themes.theme: The hidden contraction beneath the boom

insights.claim: When semiconductors and AI servers are excluded from Taiwan's export figures, exports have fallen 40% since 2022, with factory output in those sectors falling similarly.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: The single most important number in the article: strip out AI and Taiwan is in a deep export recession, meaning headline GDP badly overstates broad economic health.
insights.quote: When semiconductors and AI servers are excluded from Taiwan’s export figures, exports have fallen an alarming 40% (Opens in new window) since 2022.
insights.locator: When semiconductors and AI servers are excluded

insights.claim: Taiwan's boom has severely accentuated the dual economy dynamic characteristic of East Asian economies — bifurcation into globally dominant semiconductor and adjacent exporters versus smaller firms in traditional manufacturing and services.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: A transferable lens for reading Korean and Japanese data too: national aggregates hide divergent firm-level realities in concentrated export economies.
insights.quote: this means the bifurcation of the economy into globally competitive and indeed dominant exporters of semiconductors and adjacent goods, and typically smaller companies operating in traditional manufacturing sectors and services
insights.locator: However, Taiwan’s boom times have severely accentuated

insights.claim: Taiwanese manufacturers of machinery, metals and chemicals have been clobbered by fierce Chinese competition and struggle to match the wages offered by Taiwan's high-flying tech manufacturers.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: Twin squeeze of Chinese price competition and domestic wage competition means traditional Taiwanese industrials face structural, not cyclical, decline.
insights.quote: Manufacturers of goods including machinery, metals and chemicals have been clobbered by fierce Chinese (Opens in new window) competition

insights.claim: Around 80% of Taiwanese exports now fall into the AI hardware category, up from half before the pandemic, concentrating national exposure in a sector acutely vulnerable to technological shifts.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: A 30-point jump in export concentration in roughly five years quantifies Taiwan's single-sector risk — the number to cite when sizing downside from an AI capex pause.
insights.quote: Around 80% (Opens in new window) of Taiwanese exports fall into this category, up from half before the pandemic.
insights.locator: Around 80% of Taiwanese exports fall into this category

insights.claim: The release of new, highly competitive Chinese AI models requiring markedly fewer chips to train and run recently led markets to reprise fears that AI hardware stocks are significantly overvalued.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: Model efficiency gains are the identified transmission channel from Chinese AI releases to Taiwanese hardware valuations — a recurring, tradeable shock pattern.
insights.quote: The release of new and highly competitive Chinese AI models requiring markedly fewer chips to train and run recently led markets to reprise fears that AI hardware stocks are significantly overvalued.
insights.locator: The release of new and highly competitive Chinese AI models

themes.theme: Trade reorientation toward the United States

insights.claim: The combined effect of US tariffs, supply chain re-routing and Taiwan's export surge means Taiwan is now exporting more to the United States than to China in dollar terms — a reversal of the long-standing pattern.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: Taiwan's trade dependence has flipped toward the US, changing which economy's demand shock hurts Taipei most — and altering Beijing's economic leverage.
insights.quote: Taiwan is, fantastically, exporting (Opens in new window) more to the US than China in dollar terms
insights.locator: The combined effect of US tariffs

insights.claim: Any sustained drawdown in US AI-related capital expenditure would render Taiwan's US-over-China export figures anomalous, making the reorientation contingent rather than structural.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: Explicitly conditions the trade-flip thesis on US hyperscaler capex — track capex guidance as the single variable that unwinds the whole picture.
insights.quote: Of course, any sustained drawdown in US AI-related capital expenditure would render these figures anomalous.

insights.claim: The United States is ever more dependent on Taiwan for a sector that comprises more than half of current US GDP growth and that many in the White House believe is critical to winning the 21st century.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: If AI is over half of US growth, a Taiwan supply disruption is a direct US recession risk — the strongest economic argument against treating Taiwan as expendable.
insights.quote: which comprises more than half (Opens in new window) of current US GDP growth
insights.locator: But for the time being, there’s no denying

themes.theme: Silicon shield and the bargaining-chip question

insights.claim: TSMC is investing more than US$250 billion in the United States, with many Taiwanese suppliers in adjacent sectors like servers following suit.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: A quarter-trillion-dollar onshoring wave pulls the Taiwanese supplier ecosystem with it — watch US-sited server, cooling and module capacity announcements.
insights.quote: TSMC is investing more than US$250 billion (Opens in new window) in the United States
insights.locator: TSMC is investing more than US$250 billion

insights.claim: TSMC is highly attuned to government fears about losing Taiwan's silicon shield and will keep its most advanced production and R&D functions in Taiwan, with US facilities likely to remain very reliant on Taiwanese workers.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: Onshoring does not transfer the leading edge — the deterrence value of Taiwanese fabs persists, and US capacity remains a follower node.
insights.quote: It will keep its most advanced production and R&D functions in Taiwan.
insights.locator: TSMC, however, is highly attuned to government fears

insights.claim: Against Trump's musing that Taiwan is a very good negotiating chip in the broader US–China relationship, the economic evidence makes Taiwan look less like a bargaining chip and more like a linchpin of future US prosperity.
insights.speaker: Henry Storey
insights.so_what: Economic interdependence, not rhetoric, is the better predictor of US behaviour toward Taiwan — a reason to discount transactional-abandonment scenarios for now.
insights.quote: At present, Taiwan looks less like a bargaining chip (Opens in new window) and more like a linchpin in future US economic prosperity.
insights.locator: At present, Taiwan looks less like a bargaining chip
